title: Balancing redox equations
examples: How do I know when to use the half-equation method?
Is the ion-electron method only for acids?
What is the difference between the two balancing methods?

explain.say: Today we will learn to balance redox equations.

items: Redox reactions involve changes in oxidation states.
Balancing ensures mass and charge conservation.
We use half-equations for this process.

explain.say: First we must separate the reaction into two half-equations.
Next we balance atoms other than oxygen and hydrogen.

items: Step 1: Balance atoms (not O or H)
Step 3: Balance H with H+ ions

explain.say: Then we adjust the charges by adding electrons to the appropriate side.
Finally we multiply the two half-equations to get the full balanced equation.
In daily life, batteries use redox reactions to produce electricity.

faq.q: When do I use the ion-electron method instead of half-equations?
faq.a: The ion-electron method is essentially the same as the half-equation method.
asks: Which method is better to use?

faq.q: What if the solution is basic instead of acidic?
faq.a: If the solution is basic, you must add hydroxide ions on both sides.
asks: What if I don't have H+?
How do I change it to basic?

faq.q: Do I need to balance the atoms in the overall equation first?
faq.a: No, you must balance the atoms within each half-equation separately.
asks: Do I balance everything at once?
Which equation do I balance first?

faq.q: Why do I add electrons to one side only?
faq.a: Electrons are only added to the side where the oxidation state increases.

faq.q: If I have a complex ion, how do I treat it?
faq.a: Treat the complex ion as a single unit when balancing atoms.
asks: Can I treat brackets as one thing?
What if the ion is big?

facts: Redox reactions involve the transfer of electrons.
Oxidation is the loss of electrons.
Reduction is the gain of electrons.
In acidic solutions, water is balanced using H+ ions.

quiz.say: Balance the reaction: MnO₄⁻ + Fe²⁺ → MnO₂ + Fe³⁺ in acid.
quiz.why: The manganese changes from +7 to +2, which is a reduction, so electrons are gained.

wrong.0: This does not correctly balance the hydrogen atoms.
wrong.1: This incorrectly balances the oxygen atoms in the product side.
wrong.3: This incorrectly balances the oxygen atoms on both sides.

quiz.say: Balance the reaction: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu in acid.

options.say: Zn + Cu squared⁺ to Zn squared⁺ + Cu + 2H⁺
Zn + Cu squared⁺ to Zn squared⁺ + Cu + 2O
Zn(s) + Cu squared⁺(aq) to Zn squared⁺(aq) + Cu(s)
Zn + Cu squared⁺ to Zn squared⁺ + Cu + 2e⁻

quiz.why: The oxidation states of Zn and Cu do not change, so no electrons are explicitly added.

wrong.0: Adding H+ ions is only necessary when balancing oxygen or hydrogen.
wrong.1: Oxygen atoms are not involved in the change of oxidation states here.
wrong.3: You should not add electrons if the oxidation states remain the same.
